h1: India visa changes: Tourist visa to become Visitor visa
intro: India is planning major India visa changes that will cut the number of visa categories and rename the Tourist visa as a Visitor visa. The new system is expected by the end of 2026, but nothing has changed yet for travellers. Here’s what’s been announced and what it means if you’re planning a trip.

sections.heading: What are the India visa changes?
sections.text:
India’s Ministry of Home Affairs is simplifying its visa system. According to reports in November 2026:
- the main visa categories will fall from 13 to 9
- sub-categories will fall from 49 to 23
- application forms will be shortened, with around 65 to 70% fewer questions

The nine main categories will be Business, Diplomatic, Work, Journalist, Medical, Official, Student, Visitor and Miscellaneous.

sections.heading: The Tourist visa becomes a Visitor visa
sections.text:
The best-known change is that the Tourist visa will be renamed the Visitor visa, split into two types, V-1 and V-2. Other categories are being reorganised too:
- Medical visas into four types, M-1 to M-4
- Student visas into S-1 and S-2
- Business visas into B-1 and B-2

The changes are expected to apply to e-Visas as well as paper visas. The government is updating its online systems to handle the new categories.

sections.heading: When will the changes start?
sections.text:
The government has said visas under the new framework are expected to be issued by the end of 2026. At the time of writing, no official notification with a start date has been published.

Until it is, you apply exactly as you do now, using the current categories such as the 30-day, 1-year and 5-year e-Tourist visa.

sections.heading: What the India visa changes mean for UK travellers
sections.text:
- If you’re travelling soon, apply under the current rules. There’s no need to wait.
- There’s no indication that visas already issued will be cancelled, but the government hasn’t published details yet.
- Shorter forms should make applying quicker once the new system is live.
- Fees haven’t been announced for the new categories. We’ll update our prices if anything changes.

We’ll post an update on our [visa news](/news/) page as soon as the official notification is published.

sections.heading: Avoiding problems while the system changes
sections.text: Changes to online systems can bring short delays or technical problems. If you’re travelling over Christmas or in the new year, apply at least a few weeks before you fly, and check every detail on your form matches your passport exactly. Mistakes in names, dates and passport numbers are the most common reasons e-Visas are refused.

sections.heading: How we can help
sections.text: We’ve helped UK travellers with Indian visas since 2007. We can apply for your [India e-Tourist visa](/e-tourist-visa-india/), check your photo and documents, and handle paper visas for longer stays through our [Indian visa service](/indian-visa-application-uk/).

faqs.q: Has the Indian Tourist visa changed yet?
faqs.a: Not yet. The new Visitor visa is expected by the end of 2026, but no start date has been published. Apply under the current categories until then.

faqs.q: Will my existing Indian visa still be valid?
faqs.a: There’s no indication that visas already issued will be cancelled. Keep checking official updates before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the e-Visa affected by the India visa changes?
faqs.a: Yes, the new categories are expected to apply to e-Visas too, with shorter online forms.
Fees for the new categories haven’t been announced. We’ll update this page when they are.

faqs.q: Should I wait for the new system before applying?
faqs.a: No. If you’re travelling soon, apply now under the current categories. Waiting could leave you without a visa if the new system is delayed or has early teething problems.

faqs.q: Where can I check official India visa updates?
faqs.a: On India’s official e-Visa website and the High Commission of India in London. We also post updates on our visa news page when the official notification is published.
